stem: Which imaging study is the preferred acute investigation when raised intracranial pressure is suspected in a child?

options.text: No imaging if the fontanelle is open

explanation: CT of the brain is the preferred acute investigation when raised intracranial pressure is suspected, because it can be obtained rapidly and helps guide urgent management.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because CT of the brain is the appropriate acute imaging choice when raised intracranial pressure is suspected.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because lumbar puncture should not be done before imaging when raised intracranial pressure is suspected.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because MRI spine does not assess the acute intracranial problem described here.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because urine HMA/VMA testing is used for neuroblastoma evaluation, not acute raised intracranial pressure.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because an open fontanelle does not remove the need for brain imaging when raised intracranial pressure is suspected.
